title: The Story of the Three Apples

paragraphs.en: A few days later, the caliph decided to visit the city and question its people about his administrators' conduct. He wanted to dismiss those criticized and promote those praised. Accompanied by Ja’far and Masrur, he walked through the streets at night.
paragraphs.zh: 几天后，哈里发决定亲自前往这座城市，询问市民们关于他手下官员的表现。他打算革除那些被批评的人，提拔那些受到赞扬的官员。在贾法尔和马苏尔的陪同下，他在夜间漫步于街头巷尾。

paragraphs.en: In an alley, they met a poor old fisherman carrying a basket and net on his head and holding a staff.
paragraphs.zh: 在一条小巷里，他们遇到了一位头戴篮子和渔网、手持鱼竿的贫穷老渔夫。

paragraphs.en: The caliph asked the old man about his trade. The fisherman replied that he had been fishing all day without luck, feeling helpless and wishing to die. The caliph offered him a chance: if the fisherman returned with them to the Tigris River and cast his net for him, he would buy whatever was caught for one hundred dinars.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发问起老人的营生。渔夫回答说，他一整天都在捕鱼却毫无收获，感到束手无策，甚至希望自己就此死去。哈里发给了他一个机会：如果渔夫能带他们回到底格里斯河，并替他撒网捕鱼，捕到的东西他会出一百第纳尔买下。

paragraphs.en: Excited by the offer, the old man agreed and went back with them. He cast his net, which yielded a locked chest when pulled up. The caliph gave the fisherman one hundred dinars and instructed Masrur to carry the chest back to the palace.
paragraphs.zh: 兴奋不已，老人欣然应允，跟着他们返回。他撒下渔网，拉起后竟捞上来一个锁着的木箱。哈里发给了渔夫一百第纳尔，并吩咐马斯鲁尔将木箱带回宫中。

paragraphs.en: Upon breaking it open, they found inside a basket of palm leaves sewn with red thread. Cutting the basket, they discovered a piece of carpet and a folded woman’s cloak. At the bottom lay a young girl as fair as silver, who had been slain and cut into pieces.
paragraphs.zh: 他们打开后，发现里面用红线缝制着一篮棕榈叶。剪开篮子，又发现了地毯碎片和一件折叠的女式斗篷。底部躺着一个如同银子般美丽的少女，已被杀害并剁成了几块。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad paused her story. Dinarzad urged her to continue, but Shahrazad promised an even better tale if she lived another night.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德停下了故事。迪纳札德催促她继续讲下去，但沙赫拉兹德承诺如果再活一个夜晚，一定会给她讲述一个更加精彩的故事。

paragraphs.en: The caliph, upon seeing the girl cut into nineteen pieces, felt sorrow and anger. He turned to Ja'far, demanding vengeance for her death and threatening to hang him if he failed to find the murderer within three days.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发见那女孩被切成十九块，心中既悲痛又愤怒。他转向贾法尔，要求为她的死报仇，并威胁如果三天内找不到凶手就将他处以绞刑。

paragraphs.en: Ja'far returned to the city, troubled and uncertain. He mused, "Where can I find this killer?" Reflecting on his helplessness, he concluded, "Only God can provide a solution."
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔回到城市，心中充满了困惑和不安。他自言自语道：“我要去哪里找到这个杀手呢？”思索着自己的无力感，他感慨道：“只有上帝才能提供解决之道。”

paragraphs.en: On the third day, the caliph summoned Ja'far. When asked about the murderer, Ja'far replied, "O Commander of the Faithful, am I skilled in solving murders?"
paragraphs.zh: 第三天，哈里发召见了贾法尔。当被问及凶手时，贾法尔回答说：“万民之主，我可擅长破解命案吗？”

paragraphs.en: The caliph's anger intensified. He ordered Ja'far to be hanged and announced throughout Baghdad that he would watch the execution with forty of his Barmaki relatives.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发的怒火越烧越旺，他命令贾法尔被绞死，并在巴格达全市宣布，将与四十名巴尔马基家族的亲戚一同观看处决。

paragraphs.en: The governor and chamberlains brought Ja'far and his kinsmen to stand under the gallows.
paragraphs.zh: 总督和大臣们将贾法尔和他的族人带到绞刑架下站立。

paragraphs.en: A neatly dressed young man pushed through the crowd towards Ja’far, his bright face with dark eyes and rosy cheeks covered in a downy beard. He kissed Ja’far’s hand and confessed, "O Grand Vizier, spare me from this fate. I am the one who murdered the girl."
paragraphs.zh: 一位衣着整洁的年轻人挤过人群，朝贾法尔走去。他明亮的脸上长着一双深邃的眼睛和红润的双颊，下巴上覆盖着一层细细的胡须。年轻人向贾法尔施礼，低声说道：“阁下，求您饶恕我吧。我就是杀害那位少女的人。”

paragraphs.en: Ja’far was relieved but saddened by the young man's admission.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔松了口气，但听到年轻人的承认又感到有些伤感。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, an old man, well-advanced in years, forced his way through the crowd to Ja’far. He declared, "O Vizier and mighty lord, do not believe him. I am the murderer of the girl.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，一位年事已高的老人挤过人群来到贾法尔面前，喊道：“ vizier 和伟大的主人啊，请不要相信他。我就是那个杀害女孩的人。”

paragraphs.en: Punish me for her death." The young man cried out, "O Vizier, it was I who murdered her."
paragraphs.zh: “请您惩罚我吧。”年轻人喊道，“ vizier ，就是我杀死了她。”

paragraphs.en: The old man pleaded, "Son, you are still very young; I am an old man with enough of life. Give your life for mine." Turning to Ja’far, he said, "None murdered the girl but me.
paragraphs.zh: 老人恳求道：“儿子，你还很年轻；而我已经是个饱经风霜的老人了。你用你的生命来换我的吧。”他转向贾法尔说：“杀害那个女孩的，只有我一人。”

paragraphs.en: Hang me now before my time is up."
paragraphs.zh: “现在就处死我吧，别让我受罪了。”

paragraphs.en: Ja’far overheard the conversation and brought both the young man and old man to the caliph. After kissing the ground seven times, Ja’far presented them before the caliph.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔无意中听到了他们的对话，便将那年轻人和老人引见给哈里发。他向地面亲吻了七次后，将二人呈现在哈里发面前。

paragraphs.en: "O Commander of the Faithful," Ja’far began, "I have brought you the girl’s murderer. Each claims he is guilty."
paragraphs.zh: “忠于信仰的指挥官，”贾法尔说道，“我已经带来了那个女孩的凶手。他们各自声称自己才是罪犯。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph asked, "Which one killed her?"
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发问道：“究竟是哪一个害死了她？”

paragraphs.en: The young man confessed, "I did." The old man countered, "It was I who murdered her."
paragraphs.zh: 年轻人承认道：“是我干的。”老人反驳说：“其实是我在谋杀她。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph ordered, "Hang both of them." But Ja’far interjected, "O Commander of the Faithful, only one is truly guilty. Hanging the other would be unjust."
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发下令：“将他们俩都绞死。”但贾法尔插话说：“哦，至高无上的领袖，只有一个人真正有罪。绞死另一个人是不公平的。”

paragraphs.en: The young man then spoke, recounting his actions: "Four days ago, I killed her, placed her in a basket of palm leaves, covered her with a woman’s cloak, and sewed it with red thread before throwing her into the river. By God and His Judgment Day, punish me for her death; let me not live after her."
paragraphs.zh: 年轻人随后开口述说：“四天前，我杀了她，将她放在一篮棕榈叶中，用一件女人的披风覆盖好，并用红线缝合，然后把她扔进了河里。凭上帝和末日审判之名，惩罚我的罪行；让我在她的死后再也不得存活。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph was amazed by the young man's confession and asked, "What led you to kill her? Why did you come forward?"
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发对年轻人的供词感到惊讶，问道：“你为什么要杀她？你为什么站出来承认？”

paragraphs.en: The young man replied, "Our story is so complex that it would be a lesson even if written on the corner of an eye. Tell us what happened between us."
paragraphs.zh: 年轻人回答说：“我们的故事错综复杂，即便写在眼角的角落里也是一堂生动的课。告诉我们我们之间发生了什么吧。”

paragraphs.en: But Shahrazad was interrupted as morning approached, leaving her narrative incomplete.
paragraphs.zh: 但随着晨光渐亮，莎赫拉兹被中断了，她的讲述未能完整结束。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad resumed:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，莎赫拉兹道：

paragraphs.en: O happy King, I heard that the young man said...
paragraphs.zh: 幸福的国王啊，我听见那个年轻人说道……

paragraphs.en: The murdered girl was my wife and mother of my children. She was also the daughter of this old man, my uncle, whom I married when she was a young virgin. We lived together for eleven years, during which God blessed us with three sons.
paragraphs.zh: 被谋杀的女孩是我的妻子，也是我的孩子们的母亲。她还是这位老人——我的叔叔——的女儿，我在她还是处女的时候便娶了她。我们一起生活了十一年，在这期间，上帝赐予我们三个儿子。

paragraphs.en: Despite her illness in the first month of this year, I cared for her diligently until she slowly recovered by the end.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管她在今年一月病倒了，我依然悉心照料，直到她慢慢恢复健康。

paragraphs.en: One day, before going to the bath, she said, "Husband, I want you to satisfy a desire." I replied, "I hear and obey, even if it were a thousand desires." She asked for an apple.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，在去洗澡之前，她说道：“老公，我想满足一个愿望。”我回答道：“我听从并遵照你的意愿，哪怕是一千个愿望也无妨。”于是她要了一个苹果。

paragraphs.en: If I could just smell it and take a bite, she wouldn’t mind dying afterward. I went searching but found no apples in the city. Vexed, I returned home disappointed.
paragraphs.zh: 要是能闻一闻、尝一口，她倒也不介意就此死去。我在城里四处寻找，却一无所获。失望之余，只得垂头丧气地回到了家中。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, I searched the orchards but still found none. Finally, an old gardener told me that only the Commander of the Faithful's orchard in Basra had apples stored by the gardener. Driven by love and concern, I journeyed day and night for two weeks to return with three apples.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，我便在果园里四处搜寻，但依然没有发现。终于，一位老园丁告诉我，在巴士拉，只有忠义将军的果园里有园丁储存的苹果。怀着对他的爱与关切，我日夜兼程，历时两周，才带回了三个苹果。

paragraphs.en: When I handed them to her, she showed no pleasure but laid them aside. She suffered another relapse, lay ill for ten days, and made me worry about her constantly.
paragraphs.zh: 当我把苹果递给她时，她并没有表现出丝毫喜悦，而是将它们放在一旁。她的病情再次恶化，卧床十天之久，让我整日忧心忡忡。

paragraphs.en: One day in my shop, while trading fabrics, I noticed an ugly black slave, towering like a reed and broad as a bench. He held one of the three apples that had taken me half a month to acquire. I called out, "My good slave, where did you get this apple?"
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，在我的布店中，我正与顾客交易布料时，忽然注意到一个又黑又丑的奴隶，身材高挑如芦苇，肩膀宽阔犹如木凳。他手中握着那三个花了我半个多月才买到的苹果之一。我喊道：“好 Slave，这个苹果是从哪里来的？”

paragraphs.en: He replied, "I got it from my mistress; she was ill with three apples by her side when I visited her today. Her husband had journeyed for half a month to bring them." After eating and drinking with her, he took one of the apples.
paragraphs.zh: 他回答说：“是从我的女主人那里得到的；今天我去探望她时，她正病得卧床不起，身边放着三个苹果。她的丈夫为了给她买这些苹果，已经外出半个月了。”说完，他们一起吃了些东西喝了点水，随后他也拿了一个苹果。

paragraphs.en: Upon hearing his words, I felt a surge of anger. I locked up my shop and went home. Finding only two apples, I confronted my wife: "Wife, where is the other apple?"
paragraphs.zh: 听到这话，我顿时怒从中来。我关了店铺，回家后发现只剩下两个苹果，便质问妻子：“老婆，另一个苹果呢？”

paragraphs.en: She replied, "By God, husband, I don’t know." This convinced me that the slave had told the truth.
paragraphs.zh: 她回答说：“天哪，亲爱的丈夫，我真的不知道。”这让我相信那个奴隶说的是实话。

paragraphs.en: I took a sharp knife and silently knelt behind her, cutting into her throat and severing her head. I placed her in a basket, covered it with a woman’s cloak, added a carpet on top, and sewed the basket shut. Then, I carried the basket to the Tigris River and threw it in.
paragraphs.zh: 我迅速取出一把锋利的刀子，悄悄地跪在她身后，猛地割断了她的喉咙，将她的头颅砍下。我把她放在一个篮子里，用女人的披风盖好，又放上一块地毯，然后缝紧篮子的口。随后，我将这个篮子带到底格里斯河，将其抛入水中。

paragraphs.en: When I returned home, my eldest son was crying. He told me he had stolen one of the apples for his mother that morning. As he stood with his brothers at the market, a tall black slave snatched the apple from him.
paragraphs.zh: 我回到家时，大儿子正在哭泣。他告诉我，那天早上为了给母亲偷了一个苹果。当时他在市场上和兄弟们站在一起，一个高大的黑奴突然抢走了那个苹果。

paragraphs.en: My son pleaded but the slave ignored him, slapping him and leaving with the apple.
paragraphs.zh: 我儿子苦苦哀求，但那奴隶置若罔闻，一巴掌打过去，便带着苹果头也不回地走了。

paragraphs.en: My son fled outside the city with his brothers in fear until nightfall. He begged me not to tell my wife about this; her illness would worsen otherwise. Realizing I had wrongfully killed my wife, I wept, making my sons cry too.
paragraphs.zh: 我的儿子和他的兄弟们在恐惧中逃出了城，直到夜幕降临。他央求我不要把这件事告诉妻子，否则她的病情会加重。意识到自己错杀了妻子，我痛哭起来，孩子们也被我的悲痛所感染，跟着啜泣了起来。

paragraphs.en: My uncle, who was also her father, joined us and we mourned for three days.
paragraphs.zh: 我的叔叔也是她的父亲，他加入我们一同哀悼了三天。

paragraphs.en: This is the story of the murdered girl. By your fathers and forefathers, I beg you to avenge her unjust death on me and kill me for my mistake; I have no life left after her.
paragraphs.zh: 这是被谋杀女孩的故事。我恳求你们的父亲和祖先为她主持公道，将我置于死地以弥补我的过错；自从她的离世，我已经失去了生的希望。

paragraphs.en: The caliph was amazed by the young man's story. He vowed to execute only the guilty slave and promised a deed that would satisfy both justice and his own desires.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发对年轻人的故事感到十分惊讶。他誓言只处决有罪的奴隶，并许下一项既能满足公正又能迎合自己心愿的诺言。

paragraphs.en: Ja'far left in tears for the city, believing he faced certain death. Yet, he hoped God might save him again. He stayed home for three days, preparing his will by noon on the third day.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔泪眼汪汪地离开了城市，相信自己面临绝境。然而，他仍然希望上天能再次拯救他。他在家待了三天，到第三天中午时分已经准备好遗嘱。

paragraphs.en: A messenger arrived from the caliph, warning Ja'far of imminent execution. Ja'far wept, bidding farewell to his family and household. His daughter, whom he loved most, approached, comforting him as they said their goodbyes.
paragraphs.zh: 信使从哈里发那里赶来，警告贾法尔即将面临死刑。贾法尔泪如雨下，与家人和仆人依依惜别。他最疼爱的女儿走近，安慰着他，二人互道珍重。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, she mentioned an apple with the caliph's name in her pocket.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，她提到了一个带有哈里发名字的苹果。

paragraphs.en: Ja'far, upon feeling the round object, recognized it immediately. He cried out, "O Speedy Deliverer!"
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔一感觉到那个圆东西，立刻认了出来，脱口喊道：“速递员快点！”

paragraphs.en: Ja'far summoned the slave and confronted him with the apple's origin. The slave recounted how he found a child who had dropped the fruit in an alley. He beat the child and took the apple, despite the boy’s plea that it belonged to his ill mother.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔召来奴隶，质问他那苹果的来历。奴隶讲述了他如何在小巷中发现一个孩子不慎掉落了水果，尽管男孩央求说这苹果属于病中的母亲，贾法尔还是打了那个孩子，并夺走了苹果。

paragraphs.en: Four days earlier, the boy’s father had traveled for half a month to Basra to bring back three apples, from which this one was stolen.
paragraphs.zh: 四天前，男孩的父亲远行半个月才从巴士拉带回三个苹果，其中一个不知何时失踪了。

paragraphs.en: Ja'far was amazed by the story and led the slave before the caliph. The Commander of the Faithful was astonished, laughing until he fell over. He asked Ja'far if his slave truly caused all the trouble.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔被这个故事惊呆了，便带着奴隶来到了哈里发面前。信仰的捍卫者听了之后大为惊讶，笑得几乎滚下了椅子。他问贾法尔，他的奴隶真的制造了所有的麻烦吗？

paragraphs.en: Ja'far confirmed that it was indeed the slave's actions.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔确认那是奴隶所为。

paragraphs.en: Seeing the coincidences, Ja'far mentioned another tale involving two viziers, Nur al-Din Ali al-Misri and Badr al-Din Hasan al-Basri, which he claimed was even more extraordinary. The caliph inquired if this story surpassed their current situation. Ja'far agreed it was more amazing but would only share it under a condition.
paragraphs.zh: 看到这些巧合，贾法尔提到了另一个涉及两位 vizier 的故事，名叫努尔·阿尔丁·阿里·阿勒·密斯里和巴德尔·阿尔丁·哈桑·阿勒·巴斯里的故事，并声称这个故事更加离奇。哈里发询问这个故事是否超越了他们目前的处境。贾法尔承认这个故事确实更为惊人，但他只能在满足一个条件的情况下分享这个故事。

paragraphs.en: Eager to hear the story, the caliph demanded that Ja'far proceed. If the tale was indeed more astonishing, he promised to pardon the slave; otherwise, he threatened to execute him.
paragraphs.zh: 急切地想要听这个故事，哈里发催促贾法尔快点讲。如果这个故事果然更加惊人，他承诺会赦免这个奴隶；否则，他威胁要将贾法尔处决。

paragraphs.en: In ancient Mesopotamia, the Tigris River flowed from north to south alongside its sister river, the Euphrates. This fertile land supported thriving civilizations and mythical tales.
paragraphs.zh: 在古代的美索不达米亚，底格里斯河自北向南流淌，与它的姐妹河幼发拉底河相伴。这片肥沃的土地滋养着繁荣的文明和神话传说。
